subject: Latency & capacity runway — NimblePay pilot recommendation
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Alex Morgan <alex@nimblepay.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 19 May 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Latency & capacity runway — NimblePay pilot recommendation

Thanks again for the demo this morning, Alex — good conversation. 

Recap of the constraints you confirmed on the call:  
- Production target: p95 generation latency <= 60ms (user-facing checkout flow)
- Expected steady QPS for pilot: 35–55 qps (US region), with short bursts to ~90 qps during peak campaigns
- Typical prompt size: 120 tokens in + 80 tokens generated (avg 200 tokens total)
- Data residency: US-only, no requirement for on-prem for pilot (may revisit later)

Immediate ask from your side: recommendation on hosting mode (Hosted API vs Dedicated reserved capacity vs Private/VPC) and a clear next-steps checklist + SOW we can sign to kick off a pilot.

Proposal summary (short):
- Recommended initial path: Dedicated reserved capacity for the pilot (1x dedicated GPU pool with autoscale headroom)
  - Why: consistent p95 latency at the volumes you described; easier to tune batch/concurrency and pin quantized model variant for cost predictability.
  - Fallback: auto-failover to our Hosted API for burst periods if you want to avoid hard throttling.
- Private/VPC: not required today (no regulatory or on-prem constraint), we can revisit for prod if compliance changes.

Deliverables we propose to attach: SOW (pilot scope + timelines), 2-week benchmark plan (we run realistic traffic and measure p95/p99, cost per 1M tokens, and autoscale behavior).

Next steps I suggest:
1) You confirm pilot start window (we have capacity starting Jun 7)
2) Sign SOW (attached stub) and provide billing PO or a purchase path
3) We schedule a 1-hour kickoff to align test prompts, traffic shape, and success criteria

Attaching: nimblepay-mvp-sow.pdf (stub), pilot-benchmark-plan.xlsx (stub).

If that aligns, I’ll loop in infra and product ops to reserve the pool and draft a schedule.

—
Vanessa Ortiz

Vanessa — thanks for the clear recap. Couple quick clarifications before we move forward:  
1) The 35–55 qps is our conservative estimate; during promotions we could see sustained ~70 qps for 10–15 minute windows.
2) The checkout call is sensitive; if p95 slips above 80ms we see measurable drop-off.
3) Procurement asked whether we can start with Hosted initially while you reserve capacity, to avoid longer procurement delays on Day 0.

Two asks from our side before we sign:
- Can you give a ballpark monthly cost delta between starting Hosted with burst fallback vs Dedicated reserved pool for the pilot (rough range is fine)?
- Confirm that the fallback to Hosted will be seamless (no client code change) and whether session affinity / KV caches are preserved on failover.

Happy to do the kickoff week of Jun 7 if we can get a clear recommendation and a short SOW.

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 19 May 2026 12:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Latency & capacity runway — NimblePay pilot recommendation

Vanessa / Kim — quick internal note to capture a crisp recommendation for Alex & procurement. I took the numbers Alex gave and ran a conservative back-of-envelope for options: 

Assumptions: avg request = 200 tokens, pilot baseline 50 qps, 15 min sustained burst to 75 qps. Model: quantized Llama-3 style 70B variant (serving profile we discussed).

Option A — Hosted API w/ burst fallback (no reserved capacity):
- Pros: fastest procurement path, no upfront commit.
- Cons: p95 variability under burst; caching/kv warmup penalties can bump p95 into 80–120ms range depending on prefix reuse.
- Estimated monthly cost (pilot window): $8–12k (pay-as-you-go, depends on token usage and burst hours).

Option B — Dedicated reserved capacity (recommended for pilot):
- Config: 1 dedicated GPU pool tuned to maintain <60ms p95 at 50 qps with 10% headroom; autoscale policy to add one node at sustained >70 qps.
- Pros: predictable p95, KV cache locality, easier to tune batching and quantization profile.
- Cons: requires a short procurement commit (30–90 days typical for pilots).
- Estimated monthly cost (pilot reservation + usage): $18–26k (includes reserved baseline + modest burst usage).

Fallback notes: we can configure smart routing so that bursts overflow to Hosted API. Caveat: KV cache is not preserved across a switch from Dedicated -> Hosted (we preserve session tokens but cold-start QPS may see a latency bump for cached prompts until KV warms on Hosted). We'll mitigate by:
- pre-warming common prefixes during bench windows;
- short-term sticky routing for long-lived sessions if you want cache affinity (requires client routing header; we can implement without SDK changes via our gateway).

Recommendation & ask for Alex: start with Option B (Dedicated reserved pool) for the pilot to ensure the p95 SLA target is hit. If procurement cannot commit quickly, Option A with explicit benchmark and an SLO-based purchase clause is acceptable as an interim (we’ll log the risk in the SOW).

I’ll write a short appendix for the SOW about fallback behavior and cache-affinity tradeoffs.

—
Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Latency & capacity runway — NimblePay pilot recommendation

Alex — thanks for the quick reply and the procurement context. Finalizing recommendation below so your team can move forward: 

Final recommendation (concise):
- Start the pilot on Dedicated reserved capacity (Option B). Rationale: guarantees p95 headroom and gives us the determinism needed for checkout flow UX.
- Configure a warmup/benchmark window (2 weeks) where we run traffic that mirrors your production mix; we'll pre-warm KV caches and measure p95/p99 under the burst profile you described.
- Fallback behavior: bursts overflow to Hosted API automatically. Note the cache-affinity caveat Ben mentioned — we will pre-warm and can apply sticky routing if you want near-zero failover penalty. No client SDK change is required for the basic overflow path.

Procurement and timing:
- Proposed kickoff: Jun 7 (2-week bench Jun 7–Jun 21).
- Action for NimblePay: provide PO or procurement path by Jun 2 to secure dedicated pool. If procurement needs more time, we can stand up Hosted immediately and migrate to Dedicated once PO clears — we'll include migration milestones in the SOW.

Attached: nimblepay-mvp-sow.pdf (pilot SOW draft), pilot-benchmark-plan.xlsx (traffic shapes + success criteria). Also linking the HubSpot deal for record: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/12345.

If that looks good, please reply with: 1) PO timeline, 2) confirmation of proposed kickoff date, and 3) a primary SL contact for the pilot. I'll route the SOW to DocuSign once procurement confirms.
